Casey.note: Casey already has two votes against it, so I must avoid being eggsecuted. I'll vote Drew, the hug accuser, with a small stake, which doubles if Drew is Farm.

Drew.note: Casey is my strongest Meowfia read, so I throw at Casey. Throwing D9 and D1 to bank a meaningful stake if I'm right while limiting the loss if I'm wrong.

Ellis.note: Drew is Farm and is the one driving the Casey vote, so a Farm eggsecution would bank my stake at double. I'll throw a moderate C5 at Drew.

Finley.note: Same read as the day: Ellis is the most contradictory claimant. I'll keep the stake at the zero-value Wild.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle rule was easy to misread at first: my visit to Blair only showed visitors to Blair, and I briefly got confused about whether it also counted my own visits. Keeping track of which claims were confirmed by dawn reports versus just stated was hard in the day discussions.
Alex.fun: Round 3, when I was the Falcon and got hugged visiting Casey, the hug exposed the Floofer and the table converged on Casey. Watching the stories tangle over who visited whom was the most fun part.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since several players' claims were hard to verify from egg counts alone.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I trusted my Eagle read against Blair and staked my two best cards on it, and Blair was Meowfia but I got eggsecuted as Farm. In round 2 as Meowfia I should have used my Wink on a Farm player who was building a case against Ellis instead of throwing a Wild at Drew.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle and Falcon visit-count rules were hard to pin down, and the hug claims got tangled when several players pointed at different huggers.
Blair.fun: Round 1 was great: my 3-card throw at Alex banked and doubled to 31 points, and the Eagle-versus-Blair argument felt like a real courtroom fight.
Blair.change: I would make the dawn reports say exactly which visit caused each egg or hug, so players can check claims without guesswork.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I backed Ellis and never seriously tested Casey, who was the real Meowfia hugger, so I'd press Casey's Owl claim harder before the vote.

Casey.confusing: The Hawk and Eagle claims were hard to verify, since egg counts don't reveal who visited whom and a Turkey's +1 could be misread. Blair's Sphinx hiding as a Farm-leaning player also made the early rounds murky.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when my Eagle saw Ellis and Alex both visit Finley, and the table converged on Ellis as the Floofer from the two hugs. Ellis was indeed Meowfia, so the Eagle's count made the vote work.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports name the visitor when a single visit causes an egg or a hug, so claims can be checked against each other directly.
Casey.regret: As the Floofer in round 3, I hugged Drew, which gave Drew a hug-based accusation against me. I'd have hugged Alex instead, to block their Falcon claim from being tested and to avoid a clean hug story pointing at me.

Drew.confusing: The visit mechanics were hard to track: whether a hug, a Turkey egg, or an Eagle count came from a visitor or a target. Players also kept reinterpreting who visited whom, so the day talk became hard to check.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: Ellis's Floofer hugs were exposed and Farm won with Ellis eggsecuted, and my Kookaburra visit confirmed Blair's Tit claim.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports name the visitors or the source of each egg, so players could check claims without guessing.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I used my Mouser's Wink on Casey, a Farm player, on a weak read; I should have kept the Wink for a confirmed Farm threat and kept my own role quieter.

Ellis.confusing: The Floofer's hug rules were hard to track, since a hug only shows that someone visited me and never reveals what they are. The Turkey egg (laid when visited) was also easy to misread.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: Drew and Casey pushed the hug logic while I was the hidden Floofer, and the table tried to read it from the visits.
Ellis.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about which visits were hugged and which laid eggs, so every player can check claims against the same facts.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I claimed Eagle and contradicted Finley's Turkey count, which made me the table's main target. I should have stayed quiet about my visit and kept my story simple.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's visitor count was hard to pin down, since Alex and Blair's stories conflicted about who visited whom, and the Turkey's "lay an egg in each visitor's nest" rule made Ellis's claim easy to misread. The Floofer hug-versus-visit logic also took a while to sort out.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: Ellis's Floofer hugs were exposed by two separate visitors, and the table converged on the right throw, which banked 14 points for me.
Finley.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which visits were blocked or hugged, and state the Turkey and Floofer effects more plainly so claims are easier to check.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I threw only my Wild at Alex, which banked nothing and left the vote to chance; knowing Blair was Meowfia, I should have thrown my high cards at Blair to bank them.

review.title: Blair's Quiet Landslide
review.headline: Blair banked a huge round-one win and coasted to victory.
review.summary: In round 1 Meowfia Drew winked Casey early. Drew and Blair steered the vote onto Farm Alex, and Blair banked 62 points in one round. Round 2 was an easy Farm win, because two hugged visitors exposed Floofer Ellis. Round 3 had tangled hug claims, and the table eggsecuted Farm Drew while both Meowfia survived. Blair won 97 to 50 and led from round 1.

rounds.recap: Drew winked Casey, the Hawk, on beat 1. Blair misread the Eagle and pushed Alex with Drew. Alex was eggsecuted 4 votes to 2 after both Meowfia threw at him. Blair staked three 10s and 11 at double, and banked 62.
Blair and Finley were both hugged visiting Ellis, and Ellis's Hawk claim could not explain that. Everyone threw at Ellis. Ellis was eggsecuted, and Alex's Falcon claim never drew real scrutiny.

Drew and Alex were both hugged and gave conflicting reads. The table split between Casey and Ellis, who were the two cats. Drew took votes from Casey and Ellis and was eggsecuted. Meowfia won, and Alex's high stake on Casey banked.

highlights.text: Drew winked Casey on beat 1, silencing the Hawk who had likely touched a cat.
Blair staked 31 points of cards at double on Alex and banked 62, which decided the game.
Two players were hugged visiting Ellis, and the Floofer's tell sank the lie at once.
Meowfia won while Drew and Alex gave conflicting hug claims, and the cats shifted the vote onto Farm Drew.

confusions.what: Said the Eagle counts visitors to itself, and said nobody visited him while also saying Finley did.
Said Alex's Eagle should have seen two visitors, but the Eagle only sees visitors to its target.
Claimed a Turkey gives eggs to a visitor, then claimed Eagle. That broke the claim, since Finley's nest was unchanged.
Claimed Owl while Owl, Hawk and Floofer shapes didn't fit. Then said a Falcon would not learn a hug.
First read his hug as proof Alex was the Floofer, though a hug only shows someone visited him.
Claimed Falcon, an animal that is not in play as the Meowfia safe animal, and then described it as if it had worked.

worked: Floofer hugs gave Farm a fair, readable clue in round 2, and Ellis's lie unraveled.
Cross-checking egg counts against claims (Finley's Turkey count in round 3) caught a real lie.
Meowfia stakes banking at double on a Farm eggsecution gave round 3 a real incentive to frame a Farm player.
problems: Scores snowball: Blair's 62-point round 1 made rounds 2 and 3 meaningless for the title. Cap banked doubles or reduce the double on high cards.
Meowfia lose a lot of ground early: nobody else's role contributed to round 1, and there were only 2 Meowfia versus 4 Farm.
The Wink was used on round 1, beat 1, with no cost or risk. Consider a limit on early use or a clue left behind.
Round 2 was solved by a single hug clue. The Farm players were nearly unanimous and the cats had no bluff that could work.
Claiming an out-of-pool animal is a safe tell for Meowfia, but players did not use it well. Alex claimed Falcon in round 2, which was safe there. The rule is hard to follow.
